decision.note: The idea says users identify themselves with tokens; a client's own claim is not proof.

rejected.statement: A request names its user, and is granted when that user is authorized.
rejected.why: Simplest: the client says who it is. abs is the identity. It trusts the client's claim about its identity.

content.statement: A request is granted on behalf of a user only if its token belongs to that user and the user is authorized.
content.why: Users identify themselves with tokens they receive at login, so a decision sees a token, not a user. abs: a user is allowed a resource when some token of theirs is granted it.

sources.spec: decide => forall((t: Token.T, r: Resource.T) => decide(t, r).forall(u => holder(t) == Some(u) && authorized(u, r)))
sources.abs: decide => (u, r) => exists((t: Token.T) => decide(t, r) == Some(u))

decision.note: Checked on every call; the examples show it grants and refuses as intended.

content.statement: A decision names the user its token belongs to, and only when a grant covers the path.
content.why: GrantBased, stated for one call, so every result of the running system can be checked.

sources.post: (token, path, decision) => decision.forall(u => sessions(token) == Some(u) && grants.value.contains(Grant(u, path)))

examples: expect ("t1", Path("/a")) ⇒ Some(UserId("alice"))  given grants.bind(List(Grant(UserId("alice"), Path("/a")))), sessions.bind(Map("t1" -> UserId("alice")).get)  — Alice's token and a grant for /a: she gets in
expect ("t1", Path("/b")) ⇒ None  given grants.bind(List(Grant(UserId("alice"), Path("/a")))), sessions.bind(Map("t1" -> UserId("alice")).get)  — no grant for /b: refused

reject ("t1", Path("/b")) ⇒ Some(UserId("alice"))  given grants.bind(List(Grant(UserId("alice"), Path("/a")))), sessions.bind(Map("t1" -> UserId("alice")).get)  — access without a grant is never given

reject ("t2", Path("/a")) ⇒ Some(UserId("alice"))  given grants.bind(List(Grant(UserId("alice"), Path("/a")))), sessions.bind(Map("t1" -> UserId("alice")).get)  — a token that is not Alice's never acts for her

decision.note: Exactly the grant table the idea describes.

content.statement: Users are ids, resources are paths, tokens are strings, and a user is authorized for a path when a grant names both.
content.why: The idea defines authorization as a table of grants. The token's holder is whatever the session table says; issuing tokens is not modelled.
substitutions: authorized := (u: UserId, p: Path) => grants.value.contains(Grant(u, p))

decision.note: This is the sentence of the idea that must never be broken.

content.statement: A user is never granted access to a resource they are not authorized to access.
content.why: This is the one thing the idea says must never happen. What 'authorized' means is left open: the idea only fixes it later, as grants.

sources.spec: allows => forall((u: User.T, r: Resource.T) => allows(u, r) ==> authorized(u, r))
